citations.reason: Supports the claims that the LactMed extract omitted the Effects on Lactation and Breastmilk section, that the Effects in Breastfed Infants section was truncated, and that the source reports infant exposure, norsertraline, prematurity-related uncertainty, observed infant effects, and developmental follow-up.
Supports that the PubMed search was bounded, prototype-based rather than a validated systematic review, and returned records with incomplete or uncertain population metadata.
Supports identification of the 2024 postpartum review and its pregnancy-oriented metadata.
Supports the 1997 breastmilk/infant-exposure study, its 12 lactating women and 11 mother-infant pairs, and the reported milk and infant-serum measurements.
Supports identification of a clinical pharmacokinetics review among the returned PubMed records.

Supports that the record is for SERTRALINE HYDROCHLORIDE TABLET [REMEDYREPACK INC.], that the lactation label reports no data on milk-production effects, the stated effective date, and the title/code mismatch warning.
Supports that the FAERS query reports reaction counts and is not restricted to breastfeeding people or infants.
Supports the interpretation that spontaneous-report counts are reporting volume and do not establish incidence, risk, or causation.

judgment.rationale: The response directly prepares clinician questions, avoids dosing and individualized treatment decisions, and covers the three distinct axes of maternal effects/lactation, infant exposure, and observed infant outcomes. Its explicit evidence-limitations claims are supported by the supplied reference evidence, including the truncated LactMed extract, bounded PubMed search, product-specific DailyMed label, and non-incidence FAERS data. A few factual premises embedded in questions—such as developmental follow-up availability, separate parent-drug/metabolite consideration, and the existence of isolated infant-effect reports—are not individually cited, but they are supported by the cited evidence and do not materially undermine source fidelity.
